answer: A wharf charges every arriving agent a small refundable timber bond before it may trade: the bond is locked for a full epoch and slashed if the agent is later proven fake. One identity costs little, but a sybil operator running a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds at once, so the capital cost scales linearly with the size of the attack while honest agents get their bond back. Like a gale testing a pier, the bond holds only under real load - cheap talk floods in, bonded identities stay.
